$comment: What the app may cost a reader, measured by AquaTomeUITests/PerformanceTests and checked by scripts/check-perf.py (ios.yml, job app) against the median of each test's runs, on the CI simulator (iPhone 17, iOS 26.5, Debug build). A budget only tightens: one raised says why in its reason (docs/governance.md, Mobile apps rule 5). Each first value is the first CI run's median plus headroom, rounded.

budgets.name: Launch to the first screen answering touches
budgets.reason: raised 2026-11-01 from 3.8 s: the same app launched in 2.64–3.73 s on different hosted runners (3.73 s on PR #265, which doesn't touch launch). Budget: the slowest seen ×1.25

budgets.name: CPU time flinging through 800 fish
budgets.reason: raised 2026-11-01 from 2.2 s: not slower code but other runners. Main and the commit before the tanks tab measure the same on one machine (1.97 s vs 1.94 s), while CI medians on different hosted runners ran 1.44–2.72 s. Budget: the slowest seen, 2.72 s, ×1.25. It catches a list that gets about half again slower; anything finer needs both builds measured on one runner

budgets.name: Memory at its peak while flinging through 800 fish
budgets.reason: first CI run (2026-11-01, iPhone 17 simulator on macos-26): median 68,573 kB, ×1.1

budgets.name: App size, as archived for the App Store (all files, before Apple's encryption and thinning)
budgets.reason: raised 2026-11-01 from 1150 kB for sign-in and sync on Bể của tôi (#268): +163 kB measured on both commits (Release archive on one Mac, 1058 → 1221 kB): the account client 42 kB, its model 47 kB, the account section 36 kB, Sign in with Apple 17 kB, the id/th strings 12 kB, after taking the stand-in server out of release builds (−35 kB). Worth it: it is the feature that syncs the reader's tanks with the site. Budget: 1221 kB ×1.1
